Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

Fitted candidates (all on the same data, 126 readings):

Round 2 of 3. Decide. If you accept, 'chosen' is the candidate label, e.g. C8.

answer.feedback: Test a revised rate law or mechanism that addresses the opposing substrate residuals: C9/C40 over-predict x2 in E2 near t=5 h but under-predict x2 in E1 near t=5 h; C8 also under-predicts x2 in E2 early (worst at t=1 h) and in E3 (worst at t=4 h). C8 over-predicts E1 biomass near t=9 h. These experiment-dependent and time-localized errors suggest the current kinetics miss a response to operating conditions or changing cell state, rather than needing only a different saturation constant.
answer.reasoning: No candidate qualifies. C8 is just beyond the chi-square limit and theta1 and theta3 are strongly correlated, so they are not separately identified. C9 and C40 have severe lack of fit; C40 also has an imprecise Ki (t=0.74).
